text_blocks.snippet: A 501(c)(3) organization is a broad category of tax-exempt non-profit organizations, while 508(c)(1)(A) specifically refers to churches and religious organizations that are automatically recognized as tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) without needing to file an application with the IRS. Essentially, a 508(c)(1)(A) is a type of 501(c)(3) organization with special rules for churches.

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: A general category of tax-exempt non-profit organizations described in Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.

list.title: Purpose:
list.snippet: Organized and operated for religious, charitable, scientific, literary, or educational purposes, among others.

list.title: Tax Exemption:
list.snippet: Must apply to the IRS for recognition of tax-exempt status and file annual information returns (Form 990 series).

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Charities, educational institutions, museums, hospitals, and many other non-profits.
Definition: A specific type of 501(c)(3) organization, namely churches, their integrated auxiliaries, and conventions or associations of churches.
Tax Exemption: Automatically recognized as tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) without needing to file IRS Form 1023.
Exempt from Filing: Also exempt from filing annual information returns (Form 990 series).
Automatic Recognition: The IRS presumes these organizations are tax-exempt based on their nature as churches, etc.

Key Difference: While still 501(c)(3) organizations, churches and related entities are granted automatic tax-exempt status and are exempt from filing the application and annual returns required of other 501(c)(3)s.
